newsitem.title: UGANDA: UGANDA SEES POSITIVE DEVELOPMENTS IN ZAIRE.
newsitem.headline: UGANDA SEES POSITIVE DEVELOPMENTS IN ZAIRE.

text.p: Uganda's foreign minister has defended his government's decision to let Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila use the Ugandan presidential jet and said that developments in Zaire were positive for Uganda.
Kabila's use of the plane was widely seen as implying Ugandan government support for Kabila's rebellion.

Eriya Kategaya, foreign minister and first deputy prime minister, was quoted in the Kampala newspaper The Monitor on Friday as telling a parliamentary committee that Kabila hired the plane for a trip to talks in South Africa on May 2.
He said the government had decided earlier to cut the cost of maintaining the plane by hiring it out to heads of state and other important people.

"We were asked to fly Kabila and saw no problem. South Africa put a whole ship at the disposal of the meeting (between Kabila and Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko last Sunday). Uganda after all stands to gain a lot in future from a single flight the jet made," he added.

"The developments in Zaire are positive. Our people are already active in these areas, they are already 'okulembeka' (tapping wealth)...We need to have leaders who are concerned about development," Kategaya said.

Critics of Kabila say his military campaign has had substantial support from the governments of Rwanda and Uganda, where the leaders have ethnic links with the Banyamulenge who launched the rebellion in eastern Zaire in October.
